theory.intro: Integers follow the same order of operations as any other numbers. Keeping track of the signs is what makes these expressions harder.
facts: Work **brackets** first, then **powers**, then **multiplication and division** left to right, then **addition and subtraction** left to right.
Decide each sign as you go: same signs multiply or divide to a **positive**, different signs to a **negative**.
A minus sign can mean *negative* or *subtract*, so read each one carefully before applying the order.
steps: Evaluate anything inside brackets (and any powers) first.
Do all $\times$ and $\div$ from left to right.
Do all $+$ and $-$ from left to right.

workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Multiply before subtracting.
$5-3\times(-4)$
$=5-(-12)$
$=17$
(b) Divide before adding.
$-9+18\div(-3)$
$=-9+(-6)$
$=-15$

(a) Work out the brackets first.
$-4\times(2-7)$
$=-4\times(-5)$
$=20$
(b) Work out the brackets, then divide, then add and subtract from left to right.
$-8-(6+(-3))+12\div(-4)$
$=-8-3+12\div(-4)$
$=-8-3+(-3)$
$=-11+(-3)$
$=-14$

workedExamples.question_text:
Evaluate and explain the effect of the brackets.
(a) $(-4)^2\times3$
(b) $-4^2\times3$
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) The brackets make $-4$ the number being squared.
$(-4)^2\times3$
$=16\times3$
$=48$
(b) Square $4$ before applying the minus sign.
$-4^2\times3$
$=-(4\times4)\times3$
$=-16\times3$
$=-48$

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Evaluate $2-24\div(-4)\times(-2)$.
(b) A student writes $-3\times4+2\times(-5)=(-3\times4+2)\times(-5)=50$. Explain the error and find the correct answer.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Division and multiplication have equal priority, so work from left to right before subtracting.
$2-24\div(-4)\times(-2)$
$=2-(-6)\times(-2)$
$=2-12$
$=-10$
(b) Both multiplications must be done before the addition. The student grouped the addition with the first product.
$-3\times4+2\times(-5)$
$=-12+2\times(-5)$
$=-12+(-10)$
$=-22$
